description:
Found by s527a (2026-10-24): since PCL parses with the VENDORED PPI (vendor/PPI/lib, loaded through Pl::VendorPPI on the compiler's @INC only -- PCLPaths::program_inc drops the dir from the PROGRAM's @INC, as perl would), the runtime's compiler stamp `%p-compute-compiler-stamp` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, `%p-ppi-files`) still locates PPI through the PROGRAM's @INC (`p-find-module-in-inc "PPI.pm"`) -- i.e. it now stamps the SYSTEM PPI (or none, on a machine without one), not the PPI that produced the emission.  Pl::ProtoCache's perl-side twin (`_ppi_files`) reads %INC and does stamp the vendored files.  The Pl::ProtoCache header says the two stamps "need the same INPUTS".

Consequence: after a `tools/vendor-ppi` refresh that changes tokenization, a cached SCRIPT transpile (the runtime's cache) is not invalidated by the stamp; only the generation bump or a Pl/ change would.  No wrong answer today (the vendored lib only changes by commit, and s527a's emission is byte-identical to main), but the input is the wrong one.

Fix (cl/, so not in s527a's scope): `%p-ppi-files` should take PPI from <root>/vendor/PPI/lib when it exists (the root is known to the runtime through *pcl-pl2cl-path*), falling back to the program @INC for an installation without it.  Discriminating check: touch vendor/PPI/lib/PPI/Tokenizer.pm (mtime) and see whether `pcl SCRIPT` re-transpiles a cached script.


=== RULED s528 (Fable, 2026-10-25): FIX = s527b (in flight), one function.  %p-ppi-files mirrors the ONE loader: when <root>/vendor/PPI/lib/PPI.pm exists and PCL_SYSTEM_PPI is unset, the stamp is the vendored tree (every file under vendor/PPI/lib, sorted) and `pcl --cache-info` prints `PPI sources: <root>/vendor/PPI/lib/PPI.pm (vendored, N files)`; with PCL_SYSTEM_PPI=1, the @INC one as today.  The root is the runtime's own (the dir that holds cl/pcl-runtime.lisp -- the same resolver the module cache already uses).  Bar: the gate; a Pl/t row (the cache-info / script-cache family) asserting the stamp names vendor/PPI on a plain run and the system PPI under PCL_SYSTEM_PPI=1; everyday cold + warm; the full sweep s527b owes anyway for its shim emission change covers this too.  Confirmed on main 13720073: `pcl --cache-info` -> `PPI sources: .../site_perl/5.40.3/PPI.pm (95 files)`.  #3941 (s527b's duplicate filing) closed by reference.
subject: The runtime compiler stamp (%p-ppi-files) stamps the SYSTEM PPI found via the program @INC, not the vendored PPI that produced the emission (s527a)
